mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy or extract must be notarized in Taiwan by a notary public, then authenticated solely through Consular Legalization because Taiwan is not a party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention. For mainland China destinations, use the parallel cross-strait notarization verification channel through the Strait Exchange Foundation (SEF); never chain Apostille with Consular Legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Company Registration Information Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Obtain official MOEA extract showing no dissolution or liquidation, notarize in Taiwan, then legalize through the Taipei Economic and Cultural Office (TECO) in the destination state. If the destination is mainland China, verify the notarial certificate through SEF; Apostille is unavailable and must not be used.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the entity and Taiwan notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original resolution and power of attorney signed before a Taiwan notary; the notarial certificate then goes through Consular Legalization (or SEF verification for mainland China) as the exclusive authentication path. Apostille cannot be applied.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: MOEA-certified copy of the Articles of Association and amendments must be notarized by a Taiwan notary, followed by TECO Consular Legalization; if used in mainland China, SEF verification is the parallel and mutually exclusive path; no Apostille may be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Taiwan depository bank / AML compliance officer
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Original letter signed by branch manager on bank letterhead, notarized in Taiwan, then consular legalized via TECO for non-Apostille jurisdictions or SEF-verified for mainland China. Apostille is not available for Taiwan-origin documents.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against (i) Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission and Ministry of Justice issued terrorist-financing and AML lists; (ii) U.S. OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated sanctions list, and UN Security Council consolidated list; (iii) Chinese public security and PBOC watchlists. Beneficial owners, signatories, counterparties, and all project-site inspection clients must be screened at onboarding and continuously. PEPs, their family members and close associates require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth documentation, senior-management approval, and transaction monitoring. Automated screening tools supplemented by manual adverse-media checks; hits are escalated to the AML/CFT officer before any funding.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs - Company and Business One-Stop Application Portal (Company Name Pre-Approval and Company Registration System)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names are filed in traditional Chinese script; an English trade name may be registered as a supplementary transliteration. The four-tier check requires (1) a distinctive trade-name element, (2) a business-scope descriptor, (3) a legal-form suffix such as Limited or Company Limited by Shares, and (4) an absence of misleading or same-voice similarity with prior registered and pre-approved names. Phonetic similarity in Mandarin is treated as identity for clearance purposes.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may request a written statement of reasons and, within 15 days, file an administrative appeal through the MOEA one-stop portal or by registered mail to the Department of Commerce, attaching the rejection reference number, corrected name variants, and a legal memorandum showing distinguishability. If the MOEA maintains rejection, an administrative appeal to the Executive Yuan and, ultimately, judicial review under the Administrative Litigation Act are available. The name may be extended once for an additional six months if a substantive application for incorporation is filed before expiration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not per se prohibited by Taiwan's Company Act, but for an inspection, testing, and QC agency (ISIC 7120 / NAICS 541380), the Ministry of Economic Affairs and the National Taxation Administration apply substance-over-form review. A domestic bank will reject a virtual-office address for a corporate account where the entity cannot demonstrate a bona fide administrative base, personnel, or records. The registered office must accept legal service and be shown in the Articles of Association; a virtual office may be accepted only if the service provider supplies a lease/service agreement, mail-forwarding, meeting-room access, and the entity maintains actual business records elsewhere. Recommended model: physical registered office plus satellite virtual inspection branch office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: lease or service agreement, utility bills, employee attendance and payroll records, inspection equipment or calibration certificates, bank relationship manager references, filed business tax/VAT returns, and documentary evidence of actual QC assignments. Quantified risk: for a compliant bricks-and-mortar registered office with personnel, the annual likelihood of an unannounced on-site tax/registry inspection is low (5-10%). For a mailbox-only virtual office, the risk is high (40-60%), particularly where VAT filings show no payroll or rent expenses, and may trigger examination, denial of the registration, or imposition of penalties.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Taiwan Company Act (公司法), Articles 6, 7, 18, 22-1, 128-156, 172, 387-388; Enforcement Rules of the Company Act; Memorandum and Articles of Association of the overseas investor as applicable for corporate shareholder approval.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan – Company Registration Division and One-Stop Online Registration Portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Company Establishment Registration (公司設立登記申請書) together with the approved Articles of Incorporation (公司章程).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital is prescribed under the Taiwan Company Act for a limited company. The shareholders shall remit the declared paid-in capital in cash to a newly opened NT$ corporate bank account in Taiwan and produce a bank-issued capital confirmation certificate at the time of establishment filing. No escrow arrangement is mandated; paid-in capital may be held in a demand deposit account for operational working capital.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) The subscribers under the Articles of Incorporation hereby approve and accept their respective equity subscriptions in Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture Limited, and the Chairperson confirms receipt of the aggregate declared paid-in capital. (2) The registered office of the Company shall be the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation in Taiwan, and the Company shall file and maintain such address with the Ministry of Economic Affairs as the statutory principal place of business. (3) The following persons are appointed as first officers: [Name] as Director and Chairperson, [Name] as Finance Officer, and [Name] as Quality Operations Manager. Each officer is authorized to open bank accounts, execute registration filings, and conclude all formalities for the Company.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Name and Business Scope Pre-Authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: MOEA One-Stop Online Registration Portal (Company Name and Business Scope Advance Search System)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online application for company name reservation using the intended Chinese company name and the registered English name. The business scope shall be stated in Chinese and English as covering quality management, on-site factory audit, pre-shipment inspection, commercial inspection agency services, and related testing advisory services under ISIC 7120. If the proposed name is available, the system will issue a name-reservation certificate valid for six months.
required_dossiers: List of proposed Chinese and English company names
Proposed business scope wording in Chinese and English
Passport copies of the proposed directors/shareholders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected for identical or similar trademark conflict, file a new name choice immediately through the same portal; if the business scope is deemed ambiguous, narrow the wording to the exact ISIC 7120 services and resubmit within five working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Lawyer or notary public in Taiwan; final submission to MOEA Company Registration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the Articles of Incorporation in traditional Chinese, covering the corporate name, business scope, total authorized capital, paid-in capital structure, share classes, shareholder rights, board structure, officer appointment, registered office designation, and dissolution procedures. All subscribers or their lawful attorneys shall execute the Articles. If required by the bank or the foreign shareholder, attest the execution before a Taiwan notary public.
required_dossiers: Execution pages signed by all shareholders or authorized representatives
Board appointment minutes of the initial officers
Corporate authorization and power of attorney from the foreign investor
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA queries a non-compliant clause, the board shall adopt an amending resolution and file an amended version; minor formatting defects may be cured by submitting a supplemental correction through the online filing system.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Remittance and Bank Capital Confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan commercial bank and Central Bank of China foreign exchange reporting system for cross-border wires
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the Taiwan corporate NT$ demand deposit account using the MOEA name-reservation certificate and initial director identification. Remit the subscribed paid-in capital from abroad via SWIFT, Wire Transfer, or Wise into the corporate account. Obtain a bank capital confirmation letter or certified bank passbook summary showing the exact paid-in capital credited. If the investor remits foreign currency, file the required inbound remittance declaration with the remitting/accepting bank for the Central Bank of China record.
required_dossiers: Foreign remittance instruction and SWIFT/Wise payment receipt
Bank account opening application and signatory specimen cards
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the capital remittance is delayed or converted incorrectly, obtain a corrected remittance certificate from the bank and, if necessary, apply for an extension of the name reservation; any foreign-exchange declaration gap is cured by filing an amended declaration with supporting bank advices.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Commerce, Ministry of Economic Affairs – Company Registration Division
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the Company Establishment Registration Application electronically through the MOEA One-Stop Online Registration Portal. Attach the approved Articles, name reservation certificate, capital confirmation certificate, registered office proof, director consent forms, and officer appointment minutes. The competent authority will issue the Company Registration Certificate and Uniform Business Number upon approval.
required_dossiers: Registered office proof (lease agreement or ownership certificate)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried, respond to the MOEA deficiency notice within fifteen calendar days by uploading corrected documents; failure to cure may be remedied by filing a fresh establishment application with a new filing date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, Labor, and Statutory Business Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau, Ministry of Finance; Local Labor Office; local municipal tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Company Registration Certificate and Uniform Business Number, file the business tax registration and profit-seeking enterprise tax registration with the National Taxation Bureau. Register the company as an employer for labor insurance, health insurance, and pension contributions. If the registered office is a physical business premises, complete the local business tax premises registration and obtain the invoice block. This step enables the company to issue valid Taiwan invoices and remit withholding taxes.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate and Uniform Business Number
Labor insurance and pension employer registration forms
Seal/chop registration and invoice block application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office issues a penalty for late business tax registration, file the retrospective registration immediately with an explanatory statement to mitigate the penalty; labor registration defects are cured by completing the employer registration forms and paying the first premium within the next payroll cycle.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Bureau of Standards, Metrology and Inspection (BSMI), Ministry of Economic Affairs, Taiwan
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registered Third-Party Inspection and Testing Service Provider License (認可之商品檢驗/測試服務業登錄) for Factory QC and Audit Services

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Taiwan Environmental Protection Administration (EPA), Ministry of Environment
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category C – Exempt from formal Environmental Impact Assessment; administrative pollution-prevention registration only is required because the activity is an office-based inspection and testing agency without manufacturing or process emissions.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Office sewage discharged to a municipal sewer must comply with Taiwan Water Pollution Control Act effluent standards for pH 6 to 9, biochemical oxygen demand (BOD5) not exceeding 25 mg/L, and suspended solids not exceeding 25 mg/L. No VOC emission limits apply because the operation uses no industrial solvents or coating processes. Sample wastes and rejected inspection goods must be segregated as general enterprise waste; any hazardous test residue must be removed by a licensed waste contractor under the Waste Management Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety equipment installation and certification under the Taiwan Fire Services Act, structural load and building use safety clearance for the office and any laboratory areas under local building regulations, and an occupational workplace inspection and safe-access clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act for all dispatched factory inspection teams.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety equipment installation and certification under the Taiwan Fire Services Act, structural load and building use safety clearance for the office and any laboratory areas under local building regulations, and an occupational workplace inspection and safe-access clearance under the Occupational Safety and Health Act for all dispatched factory inspection teams.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Taiwan Ministry of Finance, administered operationally by the relevant National Taxation Bureau; principal electronic services include the Ministry of Finance eTax Portal and the Taiwan e-Invoice Platform. Corporate registration and Unified Business Number issuance are coordinated through the Ministry of Economic Affairs one-stop company registration system.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A locally incorporated company or approved foreign-invested enterprise must complete company registration and business registration before commencing business. The competent registration authority assigns an eight-digit Unified Business Number, which functions as the principal business tax identification number. The entity must register its taxable business items and fixed business premises with the competent National Taxation Bureau, submit constitutional documents, registered address evidence, responsible-person identification, investment and approval documents where applicable, bank and accounting information, and obtain business tax registration. A foreign company or branch generally files its foreign incorporation documents, branch registration documents, Taiwan agent or responsible-person details, power of attorney, and certified Chinese translations where required. Separate withholding, customs importer/exporter, labor insurance, and local government registrations may be required. Registration must be completed before taxable operations begin; changes to registered particulars must be reported within the applicable statutory period.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Taiwan does not operate a United States-style check-the-box election for ordinary companies. A limited company or equity joint venture is generally taxed as a separate legal entity on Taiwan-source income and other income taxable under Taiwan law. No general pass-through election is available for an equity joint venture. Relevant statutory choices may include approved tax accounting methods, depreciation methods, inventory valuation methods, consolidated filing or special industry regimes where legally available, and application of treaty-like arrangements under the Act for the Implementation of the Taxation Agreement between the Separate Customs Territory of Taiwan, Penghu, Kinmen and Matsu and the Mainland Area. Hybrid mismatch elections are not generally available as a general entity-classification mechanism.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Taiwan Value-Added Tax under the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: Business tax registration is generally required before commencing taxable business activity; there is no broad annual VAT registration threshold for ordinary businesses. For small-scale businesses subject to assessed business tax rather than ordinary VAT administration, the commonly applied monthly sales thresholds are NT$80,000 for goods businesses and NT$40,000 for services businesses, subject to statutory and administrative qualification rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Taiwan uses a government-regulated electronic invoice system rather than universal prior real-time invoice clearance for all taxpayers. Businesses required to issue electronic invoices must obtain invoice authorization and numbering, issue invoices through compliant software or the Ministry of Finance e-Invoice Platform, transmit invoice and deduction information within prescribed periods, and retain electronic records. B2B and B2C issuance, exchange, cancellation, allowance, and platform reporting requirements vary by taxpayer category and transaction type. Digital signatures, secure transmission, certified software, and electronic record retention may be required. Customs electronic declarations are separately processed through the customs single-window system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rated business tax may apply to goods exported from Taiwan, goods supplied to export-related businesses where statutory conditions are satisfied, services supplied for use outside Taiwan, and other expressly qualifying transactions. For on-site factory inspection, testing, quality-control, or audit services, zero-rating depends on the legal place and use of the service, the customer and contracting structure, the location of performance, and prescribed documentary evidence. Services physically performed in Taiwan for a foreign customer are not automatically zero-rated. The taxpayer must substantiate the transaction, foreign customer, service nature, offshore use or statutory export category, consideration, and receipt of payment. Input business tax refunds require valid tax invoices, customs or service evidence, accounting records, and compliance with filing and documentation rules.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Electronic Customs Export Declaration or other customs export proof for exported goods
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or other transport document
Foreign customer contract, purchase order, or service agreement
Service completion reports, inspection or testing reports, delivery evidence, and proof of offshore use where services are claimed as zero-rated
Foreign exchange receipt, bank credit advice, or other acceptable evidence of consideration receipt
Tax invoices, input tax invoices, accounting ledgers, and VAT return schedules
Import or export permits and industry-specific regulatory approvals where required
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The tax authority may deny zero-rating, assess unpaid business tax, impose interest, recover improperly refunded input tax, and require amended returns where export or offshore-service evidence is incomplete, inconsistent, fabricated, or submitted late. A fraudulent or materially inaccurate tax filing may trigger administrative fines under the Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax Act and the Tax Collection Act, generally calculated by reference to the evaded or underreported tax, with higher consequences for repeated or intentional conduct. False invoices, forged customs records, concealment of sales, or fraudulent refund claims may create criminal exposure, including imprisonment and criminal fines, in addition to tax assessment and penalties. Export proceeds and foreign-exchange evidence must be maintained in accordance with Taiwan foreign-exchange and banking rules; the 180-day period should be verified for the transaction category and current Central Bank requirements because exceptions and extensions may apply.

stage_4.account_class: Capital Escrow / Foreign-Currency + NTD Operational Accounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders Meeting resolution record and associated corporate declaration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Taiwan Company Registry, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Six months after fiscal year-end (i.e., by 30 June for a 31 December year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine of TWD 10,000 to TWD 50,000; continued non-compliance may lead to warning notices and eventual compulsory dissolution or strike-off by the central authority.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report and Financial Statements notification (for foreign-related JV filing portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Taiwan Company Registry (MOEA) and local filing agent for foreign-invested entity
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months of fiscal year-end unless extended under special circumstances
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Penalty order from MOEA; repeated failure to file may trigger suspension of certain corporate privileges and registration strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Profit-seeking enterprise income tax annual return (annual corporate income tax return)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 5th month after fiscal year-end (i.e., 31 May for calendar-year filers)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 3% of assessed tax per month up to 30 days; thereafter 0.04% daily interest and surcharge increasing to 1.5 times unpaid tax; prolonged non-filing may trigger administrative enforcement and eventual strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Unappropriated earnings tax filing (undistributed surplus earnings levy)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance Taiwan)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneous with the annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax return, 5th month after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Additional tax assessed on undistributed earnings at current statutory rates; penalty up to 200% of additional tax amount for willful non-declaration; enforced collection procedures apply.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual local registration and business license renewal filing (Business Registration Certificate)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local municipal commerce authority and Municipal Government Finance Bureau
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal by the annual business license expiry date issued by the local government; generally before 30 June annually
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalty up to TWD 20,000; continued lapse may cause suspension of business operations and deregistration risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO (ultimate beneficial owner) confirmation register filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Taiwan Company Registry, Ministry of Economic Affairs (via the central corporate register system)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after any change and confirmed at least annually at the annual shareholders' meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of TWD 100,000 to TWD 500,000 for deliberate non-filing or false UBO information; repeated violation can lead to administrative strike-off and personal liability.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Foreign-invested company annual operational return to investment commission
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEAIC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after fiscal year-end (typically 30 June for calendar-year entities)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Warning and monetary fine; continuous non-compliance may result in repatriation prohibition or limitation of foreign-investor rights and potential permit revocation.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit in Taiwan applies generally to companies with paid-in capital exceeding TWD 30 million; other companies may be required to prepare audited financial statements if revenue exceeds TWD 100 million or if deemed necessary by MOEA. For a Sino-Foreign Equity JV, audit exemption is not automatic; audited financial statements are typically required if the foreign-invested entity holds an investment approval or meets the capital threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Taiwan Financial Reporting Standards (TFRS) based on IFRS as endorsed by the Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC), with local GAAP permitted for certain small and medium-sized business cases; a Sino-Foreign Equity Joint Venture registered as a Taiwan limited company must prepare TFRS-compliant statements unless specifically classified as a small enterprise under the Company Act.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The JV must maintain a current register of ultimate beneficial owners and file an annual confirmation no later than the general meeting approval of annual financial statements. Any transfer of shares during the year must be recorded in the shareholders' register and reported within 30 days of transfer to the centralized UBO filing system. Failure to update changes within the statutory period is treated as an irregularity and is subject to MOEA fines.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 to USD 2,500 per year depending on licensed corporate service provider and registered address in Taipei or other metropolitan municipality
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 to USD 8,500 for a standard JV limited company preparing TFRS-compliant audited financial statements of the size typical for an inspection agency operation

stage_6.entry_description: Net Operating Revenue - gross inspection, testing, and quality-control service revenue net of returns, discounts, and allowances.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: The resident JV must report all Taiwan-source service revenue; no separate non-resident entry. Where services are rendered partly outside Taiwan, only the portion attributable to Taiwan activities under Article 25 or, absent a PE, the deemed-net-rate election under Article 25(1) may need separate schedules - not applicable to the JV as a resident filer.
